rates_vintage: EIA residential average, January-August 2026 (year to date)
notes: Peak sun hours are annual state averages (kWh/m2/day, latitude-tilt fixed system) derived from NREL (now the National Laboratory of the Rockies) solar-resource maps. They were not re-derived in 2026: the old latitude-tilt maps were not carried over to nlr.gov. Individual locations vary 10-25% with microclimate, elevation, shading and roof orientation.

Electricity rates are EIA average residential prices, cents/kWh, January-August 2026 year to date (Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, data for August 2026, retrieved 2026-11-03), rounded to 0.1 cent. They include fixed and delivery charges averaged over usage; a bill also depends on utility, tier, time-of-use and demand charges. US average: 18.19.

System cost per watt: $3.10 is a mid-range default. Recent US benchmarks for installed residential PV before incentives run from about $2.60/W (EnergySage marketplace quotes, 2026) to about $3.60/W (Berkeley Lab Tracking the Sun median for 2025 installs, as reported). Complex roofs and small systems cost more.

Federal Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC 25D): the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) ended it for property placed in service after December 31, 2025 (IRS: "The credit is not available for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025"). Systems installed in 2026 get no 25D credit unless new legislation restores it. Unused 25D credit from a 2025 or earlier install can still carry forward.

Leases and PPAs: the system owner (not the homeowner) may still claim the business credit under IRC 48E for systems that begin construction by July 4, 2026 or are placed in service by December 31, 2027, subject to foreign-entity sourcing rules. That can lower lease or PPA pricing; this estimator models a cash purchase.
State and utility incentives change frequently; verify at DSIREUSA.org.

defaults.federal_credit_note: The 30% Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC 25D) ended for systems placed in service after December 31, 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, so a system you buy and install in 2026 gets no federal credit.
defaults.federal_credit_lease_note: Leases and PPAs differ: the company that owns the panels may still claim a business credit (IRC 48E) for systems that begin construction by July 4, 2026 or are placed in service by the end of 2027.
